avatar.title: What your colours mean
avatar.text: Your bird's colours show the odds of what you would see if you measured it. At 70/30, measuring gives indigo about 7 times in 10 and violet about 3 times in 10. It is not a half-way color: a measurement always gives one definite answer.

gateDash.title: Gates are circuits
gateDash.text: Gates change a qubit's state. X swaps 0 and 1. H turns a definite 0 or 1 into an equal superposition, and back again. Z leaves 0 and 1 alone but swaps |+⟩ and |−⟩ by flipping the phase. A list of gates is a quantum circuit, the same kind you build in Qiskit.

ravensIntro.title: 1. Three birds, one secret
ravensIntro.text: Two Robins want to share a secret key. The Sender sends 32 notes, each holding a 0 or a 1. The Raven tries to steal the key. Each round you get a different role, so you play all three.

ravensIntro.title: 2. Matching winds
ravensIntro.text: Every note rides wind A or wind B. The Receiver guesses a wind for each note. Only notes where both Robins chose the same wind are kept. The rest are dropped. You don't need to get them all.

ravensIntro.title: 3. Peeking leaves a trace
ravensIntro.text: The Raven can peek at up to 16 notes by guessing their wind. A right guess reads the bit unnoticed. A wrong guess scrambles the note, and scrambled notes show up as errors. Storms cause a few errors too.

ravensIntro.title: 4. Check, then decide
ravensIntro.text: The Sender reveals a few kept notes to check for errors. Few errors, about what the storm forecast says: probably just weather. Many more: probably a Raven. The Receiver then picks Trust or Abort.

ravensIntro.title: 5. Points
ravensIntro.text: Trust: each Robin gets 5 per key bit the Raven didn't steal, and the Raven gets 20 per bit she stole. Abort with a Raven present: each Robin gets 50. Abort with no Raven: a false alarm, and the Raven gets 25 for the bluff.

ravens.title: Weather or Raven?
ravens.text: Reading a quantum note with the wrong setting scrambles it. On average, a spy's peek causes an error in about one in four of the peeked notes the Robins keep, so spies leave a trace. Storms cause errors too, so the Robins must judge: weather or Raven? This is the idea behind the BB84 protocol of Bennett and Brassard. Error-correcting codes by Shor, Steane, and Gottesman fight the noise.
